ShortDescription.Value: Makes the in-game weather look like the current real weather of any city you choose. Purely cosmetic.

Publish.LongDescription:
# Real Weather Sync
The world is burning. Let your cims burn with you.
## Setup
1. Enable the mod. 2. Type a city, press **Search**, pick yours from the results. 3. Done.
No coordinates, no config files, no weather codes, no manual sliders.
## Two ways to run it
**Live** - the default. Your city gets the chosen city's weather *right now*, refreshed every 15, 30 or 60 minutes.
**Follow the in-game clock** - your city replays that city's **last 24 hours** of real weather, hour by hour, matched to your own clock.
> It is 10:00 in the real world and 15:00 in your city? You get the weather Lyon actually had at its most recent 15:00. Your clock rolls on to 16:00, you get its 16:00. A full in-game day replays a full real day.
The weather slides continuously between hours, so nothing ever jumps. And the in-game clock is only *read*, never changed.
## What it does
- Takes **temperature, clouds, rain and fog** from the real city. - **Search** lists every matching city with its region, country and coordinates, so you confirm the right one instead of guessing. Cities you have used before are one click away. - **Smooth fades** between readings, driven by real time - pausing or fast-forwarding does not disturb them. Or hit **Apply Immediately** to skip straight to the new weather. - **Offline-proof.** Lost your connection? It holds the last good reading instead of dumping you into a cloudless void. - A live status panel naming the conditions, in whichever temperature unit you use. - Powered by [Open-Meteo](https://open-meteo.com/): no account, no sign-up, no API key.
## What it does NOT do
**Strictly cosmetic.** It does not touch the simulation, citizens, traffic, economy or services. It does not move the clock, the date, the season or the day/night cycle. It does not summon thunderstorms, auroras or disasters. And it writes **nothing** into your savegame.
The only things it changes are the same four visual climate values the game's own developer tools expose.
## Rain vs snow
The game decides rain-or-snow from the visual temperature - there is no "draw snow" switch for mods. So when it is genuinely snowing somewhere mild, **Show snow when it is really snowing** (on by default) nudges the visual temperature just below freezing. The displayed temperature is then a bit off; turn the option off if you would rather have an honest thermometer than honest snow.
## Compatibility
**Do not run this alongside another weather-overriding mod** - Time and Weather Anarchy, Weather Plus, Nice Weather, day/night switchers. Two mods fighting over the same climate values ends badly.
Real Weather Sync watches for the known ones and stands down if it spots one, reporting *"Incompatible weather mod active"*. That check matches on mod names, so it is a guard rail, not a guarantee. Nothing else is required to run it.
## Options nobody asked for
- **Time shift** - pull the weather from up to 24 hours into the past or the future. - **Antipode mode** - take the weather from the exact opposite side of the planet. For most of Europe that is the middle of the South Pacific. - **Take me somewhere awful** - one click to Yakutsk, Ushuaia, Death Valley, Cherrapunji and other places nobody would choose to live. Also the fastest way to see proper snow. - **Opposite day** - warm becomes cold, clear becomes overcast, dry becomes soaking.
## Privacy
Two things leave your PC: **the city name you type** (to Open-Meteo's geocoder) and **the coordinates it returns** (to its forecast endpoint). That is it. No telemetry, no analytics, no identifiers.
## Licence
MIT, source on [GitHub](https://github.com/merrinaf-tech/Real-Weather-Sync). Weather and geocoding data by [Open-Meteo](https://open-meteo.com/), licensed [CC BY 4.0](https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0/).
Publish.ChangeLog:
# 1.2.0
Two more entries under **Options nobody asked for**. Both purely cosmetic, and the weather mapping itself is unchanged.
## Antipode mode
Takes the weather from the point on the exact opposite side of the planet from your city. For most of Europe that is the middle of the South Pacific, so expect a lot of grey ocean drizzle.
Your city stays the one you picked - only the coordinates sent to the weather service are mirrored.
## Take me somewhere awful
One click and your city gets the weather of somewhere nobody would choose to live: Yakutsk, Longyearbyen, Ushuaia, Reykjavik, Mount Washington, Death Valley or Cherrapunji.
There is a practical side to this one: it is by far the quickest way to see snow, fog or a proper downpour without waiting for the weather at home to oblige. The coordinates are built in, so picking a preset needs no lookup at all.
It resets to None when you restart - it is an action, not a setting - but the city it picked is remembered like any other.
---
# 1.1.0
## Follow the in-game clock (off by default)
The headline feature. Normally the mod shows the chosen city's weather right now, as one reading. Turn this on and it instead walks that city's **last 24 hours** of real weather, picking the hour that matches your in-game clock.
It is 10:00 in the real world and 15:00 in your city? You get the weather that city actually had at its most recent 15:00. Your clock rolls on to 16:00, you get its 16:00. A full in-game day replays a full real day, in order, instead of holding one frozen snapshot.
- The weather slides continuously between the two bracketing hours, so nothing ever jumps. Fades are not involved, so the transition settings and the manual time shift are disabled while this mode is on. - The in-game clock is only **read**, never changed. Time, date, season and the day/night cycle stay exactly as the game set them. - It costs no extra data: those hourly readings were already part of the request.
## Pick your city instead of guessing
- New **Search** button lists every matching city with its region, country and coordinates, so you can confirm you got the right one before applying it. - New **Recent cities** dropdown remembers the last 10 cities you used. Switching back is one click and needs no lookup.
## Faster control
- New **Apply Immediately** button refreshes and jumps straight to the new weather, skipping the fade. It also cuts short a transition already running. - The transition length is now a slider (0-600 s) instead of being fixed at 120 seconds.
## Clearer status
- The status panel now names the conditions - "Light drizzle", "Heavy snow", "Fog" - instead of only showing a WMO code number. - Temperatures follow the unit you picked in the game's own interface settings: Celsius, Fahrenheit or Kelvin.
## Options nobody asked for (new section)
- **Time shift**: pull the weather from up to 24 hours into the past or the future. - **Opposite day**: mirror the weather. Warm becomes cold, clear becomes overcast, dry becomes soaking. Fog is left alone, because permanent fog just hides the city.
## Also
- Source code is now public: https://github.com/merrinaf-tech/Real-Weather-Sync - The description has been tightened up. - No change to how the weather itself is calculated. Still strictly cosmetic, still writes nothing to your savegame.
